title: Kyrgyz singers tell the Manas epic without a lute
body: In the Kyrgyz oral tradition, the long Manas epic is narrated by a solo performer. Shorter epics may be presented with the komuz, a Kyrgyz lute with three strings.
takeaway: Within one storytelling tradition, length and genre help determine what the audience hears alongside the words.
source: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, Art of Akyns
visual: a storyteller seated on a rug with an unused three-stringed komuz nearby

title: Jamdani weavers put extra threads only where a motif needs them
body: In Bangladeshi jamdani, weavers add small portions of extra thread across the fine base cloth. The pattern threads need not run all the way from one side of the loom to the other.
takeaway: Local extra threads let a pattern stand out against a cloth that stays fine between its motifs.
source: Bangladesh's UNESCO nomination for the Traditional Art of Jamdani Weaving (2013)
visual: a hand guiding a small bobbin through fine cloth on a loom
